concept.title: Who can see your tree
concept.shortdesc: Your tree is yours: you decide who gets a copy, and your keeps it safe.

conbody.p: Your tree is yours. does not send it anywhere. Nobody who makes can see it.
You decide what goes in your tree, where you keep it and who gets a copy. That makes you the data controller for the people in it. This includes any who are still alive.

section.title: Copies that your device makes
section.p: Your can back up the files of apps to iCloud. Your trees go with them. iCloud keeps this copy under your own account.
To see whether it is on, open the Settings app. Choose your name, then iCloud, then iCloud Backup.
A computer can also back up your when you connect it. That copy is kept on the computer.
Your makes these copies, not . Nobody who makes can see them.

section.title: Copies that you save
section.p: A copy that you save goes where you choose. shows how. If you save it in iCloud Drive, or in another folder that is kept in step with a service, that service keeps a copy too. It keeps it under your account.

section.title: Your files are not locked by
section.p: does not encrypt your trees. They are ordinary files. What keeps them safe is your .
Your encrypts its files once it has a passcode. Keep a passcode on it.
If you give someone a copy of a tree, they can read all of it.
